annotations.title: He that shal ouercome.
annotations.text: In al these speaches to diuers Bishops and their Churches, <mn>◦</mn> he continually encourageth them to constancie in faith and good life, by setting before their eies the reward of the next life. And yet the Caluinists would haue no man do good in respect of such reward.

notes.text: Doing wel in respect of reward.

annotations.title: Adore before thy feete.
annotations.text: ◦ You see this word of adoration is in Scriptures vsed for worship of creatures also, and that to fall before the feete of holy men or Angels for duety and reuerence, is not idolatrie, except the proper honour due to God, be giuen vnto them. See the Annotations vpon the 19 & 22 Chapter concerning the Apostles prostration before the Angel. And the Aduersaries euasion, saying that the adoration was of God onely: and that, before the feete of the partie, signifieth nothing els but, in his presence, is false and against the phrase of Scriptures. as 4 Reg. 4. where the Sunamite adored Elisæus, falling downe before his feete, and 4 Reg. 2. the sonnes of the Prophets adored him in the same sort. and here this adoration can not be meant but of the Bishop or Angel of Philadelphia, because he promiseth this honour as a reward, and as an effecte of his loue towardes him, saying, And they shal know that I haue loued thee. And that which he saith in the 22 Chapter, I fel downe to adore before the feete of the Angel: the very same he expresseth thus in the 19 Chapter, I fel before his feete to adore him: making it al one, to adore before his feete, and to adore him.

annotations.title: That no man take thy crowne.
annotations.text: That is, his crowne of euerlasting life and glorie, if he perseuere not to the end in faith & good workes: <mn>◦</mn> otherwise an other shal enter into his place, as Mathias did both to the dignitie of the Apostleship, & to the heauenly crowne due for the wel vsing and executing of the same function: which Iudas might and should haue had, if he had perseuered to the end. and as the Gentiles came into the grace and place of the Iewes. Other difficulties concerning this kinde of speache are resolued in Schoolemen, and are not here to be stoode vpon.

notes.text: Perseuerance in good & continuing to the end.

annotations.title: Lukewarme.
annotations.text: Zeale and feruour is commendable, specially in Gods cause: <mn>◦</mn> and the Neuters that be neither hote nor cold, are to Christ and his Church burdenous and lothsome, as lukewarme water is to a mans stomake, prouoking him to vomite. and therfore he threateneth to void vp such Neuters out of his mouth.
